items.question: What supreme attainments make a practitioner dear to the yoginis?
premises: Enjoyment is a possible attainment.
Liberation is a possible attainment.
Great accomplishment is a possible attainment.
items.inference: One who attains enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment becomes dear to the yoginis.
items.plain_english: He may become dear to the yoginis through enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment.

items.question: Which chapter concludes upon emergence from the moon island?
premises: The setting is emergence from the moon island.
A chapter is being identified.
The chapter is the ninth.
items.inference: The ninth chapter concludes with emergence from the moon island.
items.plain_english: The ninth chapter, having emerged from the moon island.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self in this practice?
premises: The self is the object of visualization.
The self is surrounded by fire.
The self stands on one foot.
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: Visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What request is made to the deity regarding the determination of knowledge?
premises: The speaker addresses the deity.
The speaker seeks the determination of knowledge.
The speaker asks for it to be made manifest now.
items.inference: The deity is asked to reveal the determination of knowledge to the speaker today.
items.plain_english: O God, make manifest to me today the determination of knowledge.

items.question: What division of the eight octads is sought for complete understanding?
premises: There is a division of eight octads.
Complete knowledge of this division is desired.
The understanding sought is endless in scope.
items.inference: The speaker seeks to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.
items.plain_english: And to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How can the wheel in the secret place be quickly accomplished?
premises: There is a wheel in a secret place.
Quick accomplishment of this wheel is possible.
Bhairava is addressed regarding this method.
items.inference: The question seeks the means by which the wheel in the secret place is quickly accomplished.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, how is the wheel in the secret place quickly accomplished?

items.question: How does Bhairava respond to the great goddess's rare question?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval.
The great goddess has asked a question.
The question concerns something hard for gods to obtain.
items.inference: Bhairava praises the great goddess for asking about a matter rare even among the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess! I have been asked about something hard to obtain even by the gods.

rows.grounds: state or location of the brahmarandhra

items.question: Which syllables are assigned to the brahmarandhra and the forehead?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with a specific location.
The syllable laṃ is associated with another location.
These locations are the brahmarandhra and the forehead.
items.inference: The syllable kṣa corresponds to the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ to the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form but may indicate the forehead region generally.
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

rows.grounds: in the region of the throat

items.question: Which syllables are assigned to the throat region and the heart?
premises: The syllable ṣa is associated with a bodily region.
The syllable śa is associated with another bodily region.
These regions are the throat and the heart.
items.inference: The syllable ṣa corresponds to the throat region and the syllable śa to the heart.
items.plain_english: Then the syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is in the heart.

items.question: What instruction follows the declaration of the place-wheels?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared.
Their meditation remains to be taught.
The beloved is asked to listen.
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teacher instructs the beloved to hear their meditation.
items.plain_english: The place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus associated with the first octad described?
premises: There is a divine lotus.
The lotus has eight spokes.
The lotus is adorned by the first octad.
items.inference: The divine lotus is eight-spoked and adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: A divine eight-spoked lotus, adorned by the first octad.

rows.grounds: ordinary social duties; final nasal shows sandhi before ca

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner adopt through sustained meditative practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equal mind.
Village duties represent ordinary social obligations.
Abandonment of such duties is prescribed.
items.inference: Through practice, one who becomes equal-minded should abandon village duties.
items.plain_english: Through practice, becoming equal-minded, one should abandon village duties.

items.question: What powers arise in this context for the beloved practitioner?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is mentioned.
Paralysis of bonds is mentioned.
These are presented as attained results.
items.inference: The practitioner gains knowledge of distant hearing and the power to paralyze bonds.
items.plain_english: Knowledge of distant hearing, and likewise the paralysis of bonds, O beloved.

items.question: What further attainments are briefly stated for the goddess?
premises: Immortality is mentioned as an attainment.
Transformation is mentioned as an attainment.
The statement is given in brief.
items.inference: In brief, immortality and transformation are attained.
uncertainties: The exact nature of parivartanam is not specified.
items.plain_english: Likewise, O goddess, immortality and transformation, in brief.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled center characterized in meditation?
premises: A second center is described.
It is eight-petaled.
It is illuminated by meditation on fire.
items.inference: The second eight-petaled center is well illuminated through fire meditation.
items.plain_english: The second is eight-petaled and well illuminated by meditation on fire.

rows.grounds: of one whose mind is absorbed

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes absorbed in one-pointed meditation.
Form can be assumed in many ways.
This ability is produced by that mental state.
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

items.question: What destructive power is attributed to the practitioner when angered?
premises: The practitioner may become angry.
The entire triple world is within scope.
Both moving and unmoving beings are included.
items.inference: When angry, the practitioner may destroy the entire triple world with all moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he may destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is identified.
Nine principles are specified.
The wheel acts as a liberator.
items.inference: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.
uncertainties: The specific set of nine tattvas is not named here.
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual benefits result from this practice?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is mentioned.
Seeing from very far away is mentioned.
Both are presented as resulting benefits.
items.inference: The practice brings the removal of wrinkles and grey hair and the ability to see from very far away.
items.plain_english: The destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise seeing from very far away.

rows.grounds: contemplative absorption; final nasal shows sandhi before ca

items.question: What disciplined practice is prescribed for assuming many forms in solitude?
premises: The practitioner should be in solitude.
Many forms can be made.
The practitioner must be intent on meditation.
items.inference: In solitude, one intent on meditation should practice assuming many forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on that, make many forms and practice meditation.

items.question: What result comes from unwavering devotion to constant practice?
premises: Constant practice is undertaken.
The practitioner is intent on that practice.
Immortality is produced as a result.
items.inference: One intent on constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: What consequence follows from daily abstention from food in this practice?
premises: Daily non-eating is practiced.
Age-related death is the subject.
A future outcome is stated.
items.inference: Through daily non-eating, one will go to death by aging.
uncertainties: The intended sense may be paradoxical or technical; the literal reading suggests undergoing age-death.
items.plain_english: Indeed, by daily non-eating, one will go to death by aging.

items.question: What bodily transformation results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: Constant practice is performed through yoga.
A duration of two times eight years is indicated.
A specific bodily form results.
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What cosmic effect follows from continually contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: A smoke-colored form is contemplated.
The contemplation is continual.
The triple world is affected.
items.inference: By continually contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world.
uncertainties: The object visualized as smoke-colored is not explicitly named.
items.plain_english: Always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world, O beloved.
